hook: Jerome Friedman trained as a physicist, earning a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley before working as a research physicist in high-energy physics. In 1972 he joined the Stanford Computation Research Group, and in 1982 he was appointed a professor of statistics at Stanford University. With Leo Breiman, Richard Olshen and Charles Stone he co-developed Classification and Regression Trees (CART), published in 1984, and in 1991 he introduced Multivariate Adaptive Regression Splines (MARS) in the Annals of Statistics. In 2001 he published Greedy Function Approximation, formalizing gradient boosting machines as a general method that later became central to widely used tools for structured data prediction. He also co-authored the textbook The Elements of Statistical Learning with Trevor Hastie and Robert Tibshirani, and is now Professor of Statistics, Emeritus, at Stanford.

achievements.title: Classification and Regression Trees (CART)
achievements.impact: Co-developed with Leo Breiman, Richard Olshen and Charles Stone, a decision tree methodology for classification and regression published as a book in 1984 that became a standard statistical tool.

achievements.title: Multivariate Adaptive Regression Splines (MARS), 1991
achievements.impact: Introduced a flexible nonlinear regression method in the Annals of Statistics, extending spline-based approximation beyond simple decision trees.

achievements.title: Gradient boosting machine, 2001
achievements.impact: Formalized gradient boosting as a general function approximation method in Greedy Function Approximation, now underlying widely used tools such as XGBoost and LightGBM.

achievements.title: The Elements of Statistical Learning
achievements.impact: Co-authored a foundational statistics and machine learning textbook used widely in graduate courses worldwide.
